- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above prior peak or use 3-day moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) within 3–5 days, model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 1–4% per negative sentiment day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often overfits recent volatility; use 14-day EWMA instead of 30-day forecast for smoother correction.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 3+ consecutive days), model may be overconfident; apply 2–5% downward correction for next 3 days, especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.
